The FOMC statement is modestly dovish via a 25 bp cut and balanced-risk guidance, but the October 2024 SLOOS points to a still-restrictive bank credit channel that tempers the easing signal. Banks continued to tighten C&I standards for small firms and reported weaker small-firm loan demand, while standards were largely unchanged for large and middle‑market firms. CRE credit remained tight across most categories, though large banks kept construction/land development standards unchanged and eased somewhat for multifamily. On households, banks tightened for subprime borrowers, while RRE and HELOC standards were broadly unchanged; consumer credit signals were mixed. Foreign banks reported stronger C&I demand with unchanged standards, offering a modest offset. Net: the cut should support debt service and activity over time, but SLOOS credit headwinds—especially for small businesses and CRE—mute the near‑term impulse, leaving the tone slightly positive but restrained.
